info.title: RoutineHub API
info.summary: Official HTTP API for RoutineHub — shortcuts and the Claude registry (prompts, skills, plugins).
info.description:
The official RoutineHub v1 API.

## Authentication
Most endpoints are authenticated with an **API key carried as a path segment**, e.g. `GET /api/v1/<api_key>/shortcuts`. Generate or rotate your key on the RoutineHub **Settings → API** page; generating a new key invalidates the old one. Store the key on your own machine, never in a shared repo. A few endpoints are public (the latest-version lookup) or use a separate HubSign key (`/sign-shortcut`).

## Response envelope
Every JSON response uses a `result` field: `{"result": "success", ...}` or `{"result": "error", "message": "..."}`. Form-validation errors also include an `errors` object keyed by field name.

## Status codes
The newer **registry** endpoints (skills/prompts/plugins) use standard HTTP status codes: `201` created, `400` invalid, `401` bad key, `404` not found / not yours, `409` duplicate content, `429` rate-limited. The older **shortcut** endpoints are legacy: most of them return **HTTP 200 even on failure** — always check the `result` field rather than the status code for those.

## Rate limits
Registry publishing is capped per day per account: skills 5, prompts 10, plugins 5, and 20 new versions/day. Exceeding a cap returns `429`.

tags.name: Updater
tags.description: The free RoutineHub Updater: one call that tells a phone which of its shortcuts have a newer version on RoutineHub. Public, no key. The open version manifest it reads is documented at https://routinehub.co/docs/updater/.

tags.name: Problem reports
tags.description: Private problem reports from a person to a listing's dev. A shortcut drops a draft; the person sends it from Safari, signed in.

tags.name: AI
tags.description:
Ask a model from inside a shortcut. Apple's "Use Model" action needs iOS 26 and an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, so a shortcut built on it does nothing on an older phone. This route answers from RoutineHub instead, over a plain Get Contents of URL — an action that has shipped since iOS 13.

The shortcut carries no model API key, because the key is ours. The person running it sends their own RoutineHub API key and must be an active member. Rolling out behind a switch: until it is on, this route answers 404.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Publish Claude Skills to the registry.

tags.name: Prompts
tags.description: Publish Claude Prompts (slash commands) to the registry.

tags.name: Plugins
tags.description: Publish Claude Plugins (bundles of skills/prompts) to the registry.

tags.name: Boxes
tags.description: Members only: your own Linux box on Google Cloud, created and destroyed over your API key (the same key as the registry API) or the MCP server. Rolling out behind a switch: until it is on, every Boxes route answers 404. Non-members get 403 "Boxes are a member perk." A box carries your registered SSH keys under your RoutineHub username, lives at most 8 hours, and deletes itself at its deadline.

tags.name: Key Vault
tags.description:
Your API key never ships inside your shortcut. A member developer stores a third-party API key on RoutineHub, points a route at an allowlisted service, and their published shortcut asks us for the ANSWER instead of carrying the key — so the `.shortcut` file anyone can download has nothing worth stealing in it.

These two routes are what the PUBLISHED shortcut calls, and both are keyless: the caller is a stranger's phone, and the install token is the only credential it ever holds. Creating keys and routes happens in the browser at https://routinehub.co/vault/, on your normal login.

Only services on the published allowlist can be called, and only over https. Rolling out behind a switch: until it is on, every Key Vault route answers 404.

tags.name: Apps
tags.description:
Members only: live logic for a shortcut, so it never needs reinstalling. Point one of your shortcuts at your own https server (a Cloudflare Worker, Vercel, anything with a URL); RoutineHub gives it a front door at `https://<you>-<app>.apps.rhub.pro/` and a generated loader shortcut. The front door checks each phone's install token, rate-limits it, and forwards the call with signed `X-RH-*` headers (`X-RH-Shortcut`, `X-RH-Version`, `X-RH-Install`, `X-RH-Entitled`, `X-RH-Timestamp`, `X-RH-Signature` = hex HMAC-SHA256 with the app secret over `METHOD
path?query
X-RH-Timestamp
sha256(body)`). Three live apps per member. Rolling out behind a switch: until it is on, every Apps route answers 404. Non-members get 403 "Live logic is a member perk."

get.description: Returns every shortcut owned by the account that the API key belongs to, keyed by shortcut name.

200.description: Map of shortcut name to id + published flag. NOTE: a bad key also returns 200 with `result: error`.

post.summary: Create a shortcut (with its first version)
post.description: Creates a new shortcut AND its first version in one call, from an iCloud share link you already have (Share > Copy iCloud Link in the Shortcuts app — minting the link needs a real Apple device). Draft by default; pass published=true to go live at once. Optional price_usd + payout put it on sale in the same call; a rejected price returns 400 and creates nothing. Submitted as form fields, not JSON.

link.description: iCloud share link for the first version.

published.description: true to publish immediately. Default false (draft).

price_usd.description: Optional: sell it from day one, e.g. "4.99" (min $0.99, max $100000, 2 decimals).

payout.description: Payout rail when price_usd is set; required only when both rails are onboarded.

201.description: Created. Returns the shortcut's id (use it for every other shortcut endpoint), url, latest_version, and the sale state.

400.description: Invalid link (not iCloud / already in use), invalid metadata (an errors object per field), or a rejected price. Nothing is created.

403.description: The account is restricted from publishing.

post.summary: Set or clear a shortcut's price
post.description: Change ONLY the price of a shortcut you own — both payout rails (card via Stripe, USDC on Base), one-time or recurring. The shortcut-side mirror of the registry price endpoint: touches pricing and nothing else, so it can never blank the listing. Send price_usd "0" to make it free again.

price_usd.description: Price as a plain 2-decimal string, e.g. "1.99" (minimum $0.99, maximum $100000). Amounts like "1.999" are rejected with 400. Send "0" to make the shortcut free again.

payout.description: Required when price_usd > 0 and both payout rails are onboarded; otherwise the onboarded rail is used.

200.description: The updated sale state (price_usd and payout are null after clearing).

400.description: Missing/invalid price_usd, unknown payment_type, or the chosen payout rail is not onboarded (the message names the rail and where to set it up).

404.description: No shortcut with that ID under your account.

post.description: Adds a new version to a shortcut you own. Submitted as form fields, not JSON.

version.description: Version label, e.g. 1.2. Must not duplicate a version already in review/approved.

200.description: `result: success` with a message on success, or `result: error` with a reason (legacy: errors are also 200).

post.description: Publishes a shortcut you own. It must already have at least one version.

200.description: `result: success` on success; `result: error` (still 200) if it has no version or is already published.

post.description: Unpublishes a shortcut you own.

200.description: `result: success` on success; `result: error` (still 200) if it was already unpublished.

get.summary: Get the latest version of a published shortcut (public)
get.description: Public — no API key required. Returns the latest version metadata of a published shortcut. Sends permissive CORS headers so it can be called from the browser. Updater apps: pass a valid API key (the `api_key` query parameter or `RoutineHub-Api-Key` header — generate one under Settings → API) and `URL` will be a short-lived signed download link that redirects straight to the shortcut file. Without a key, `URL` is the shortcut's RoutineHub page.

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: Optional. A valid RoutineHub API key (Settings → API). Authenticated callers get a working, short-lived signed download link in `URL` instead of the shortcut page. Fetch a fresh link per update check — links expire about an hour after minting.

URL.description: Where to send the user. For API-key-authenticated callers and approved updater partners: a short-lived signed download link that redirects to the shortcut file. Otherwise: the shortcut's RoutineHub page URL. Paid shortcuts always return the page URL so the purchase flow runs.

post.summary: Match installed shortcut names to RoutineHub listings (public)
post.description:
Public — no API key required. Send the names of the shortcuts on a device (the Shortcuts action Get My Shortcuts) and, optionally, the open version manifest (`iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/RoutineHub/versions.json`, `{"<shortcut id>": "<installed version>"}`). For each name the answer is one listing, several listings to pick from (top 5 by downloads, unless the manifest names exactly one of them), or nothing (the name is left out). Names match exactly, ignoring case, against published listings with an active author; private listings are never matched.

Per listing the fields are the ones `GET /shortcuts/{id}/versions/latest` already returns, and `download` follows the same rules: a short-lived signed download link for trusted updater callers (send the `X-RoutineHub-Updater` header, or a valid API key), the shortcut page otherwise, and always the page for a paid shortcut so the purchase flow runs.

The Shortcuts app sends a list placed in a JSON text field as newline-separated text, and a file as its text: both forms are accepted for `names` and `manifest`.

Rolling out behind a switch: while the Updater is off, this route answers 404.

parameters.name: X-RoutineHub-Updater
parameters.description: Optional. Sent by the RoutineHub Updater shortcut. Marks the caller as a trusted updater, so `download` is a signed download link rather than the shortcut page.

names.description: Up to 200 shortcut names (duplicates count once). A JSON array, or one string with a name per line.

manifest.description: Optional. The version manifest: shortcut id -> installed version. A JSON object, or its JSON text. Malformed entries are ignored.

200.description: What matched. Names with no listing are left out.

download.description: Same rules as `URL` from versions/latest: a short-lived signed download link for trusted updater callers, otherwise the shortcut page; always the page for a paid shortcut.

installed.description: The manifest's version for this id, when it has one.

behind.description: True when `installed` is older than `latest_version` (numeric compare, so 1.10 is after 1.9).

choices.description: Several listings share this name: the top 5 by downloads.

menu.description: The same data ready for a Choose from List: label -> {id, version, open}. Updates first, then shortcuts the manifest doesn't know yet, then each listing of an ambiguous name. Up-to-date shortcuts are left out.

post.summary: Drop a problem report draft for a listing (public)
post.description:
Public, no API key. The RoutineHub Reporter shortcut, or a dev's own debugger shortcut, sends what went wrong on a listing. Nothing is a report yet: the answer carries a one-time `claim_url`. Open it in Safari, where the person is signed in to RoutineHub; they read the scrubbed copy and press Send. Only then does it reach the listing's dev, privately. Unclaimed drafts are deleted after 60 minutes.

Before anything is saved we remove what we can spot: email addresses, phone numbers, user and app folder paths (the file name is kept), URL query strings, long key-like strings, IP addresses and GPS coordinates. This is best effort; the person reads it before sending.

Limited per network address (10 a minute, 100 a day by default); over the limit answers 429 with `Retry-After`. The listing must be published, not retired, and its author active. Rolling out behind a switch: while it is off, this route answers 404.

version.description: The version the person has, as they typed it.

note.description: What went wrong, in the person's words.

log.description: Pasted log text. 20 KB at most.

201.description: Draft saved. Open `claim_url` in Safari to send it.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the draft is deleted.

redactions.description: How many private things were removed.

400.description: Bad JSON, an empty report, a note over 1,000 characters, or a listing that is not published.

404.description: No listing has this id, or the feature is off.

429.description: Too many reports from this network. See `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Send a prompt, get text back. Works on any iOS version that has Get Contents of URL, which is every version since iOS 13.

Authenticate with your RoutineHub API key in the `X-RoutineHub-Key` header (the same key the registry API and MCP server take). The key may also travel as `key` in the body or query string, for Shortcuts actions that cannot set a header.

The answer is plain text by default, so it drops straight into a Shortcuts text variable. Ask for `Accept: application/json` or add `?format=json` to get it wrapped instead.

Errors are always JSON, even in text mode, so a shortcut can never print an error sentence as if it were the answer.

Membership is required: a valid key belonging to a non-member answers 402 with an upgrade URL. Two ceilings apply per UTC day, one per member and one across the site; a failed call still counts, because it still cost a request.

parameters.name: X-RoutineHub-Key
parameters.description: Your RoutineHub API key, from https://routinehub.co/settings. Required unless the key is sent as `key` in the body or query.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `json` to get the answer wrapped in JSON.

prompt.description: The question or text to work on.

system.description: Optional. Replaces the default instruction, which asks for brief plain text with no Markdown.
system.example: Answer as a friendly weather reporter.

key.description: Your API key, if you cannot set the header.

200.description: The answer. Plain text by default; JSON when asked for.

text/plain.example: An Apple Shortcut is a saved sequence of actions.

post.description:
Public — no API key required, and deliberately so: the caller is the phone of someone who installed a developer's shortcut, and requiring a RoutineHub account would make the vault unusable.

Call this once, on the shortcut's first run, and keep the token. It is worth nothing anywhere else on RoutineHub: it opens exactly one route, is revocable on its own, and carries none of the publishing, pricing, MCP or Boxes access a RoutineHub API key does. **A shortcut must never ask its user for their RoutineHub API key** — that key is unscoped and grants everything that account can do.

Rolling out behind a switch: while the Key Vault is off, this route answers 404.

parameters.name: route_id
parameters.description: The route's id, shown on the developer's /vault/ page.

post.summary: Ask the route's question; RoutineHub adds the key
post.description:
The shortcut asks for the ANSWER, not the key. RoutineHub decrypts the developer's stored credential, adds it to the request, calls the upstream, and passes the reply back — so the credential never reaches the device and cannot be read out of the shortcut file.

The developer fixes the service and the base address when they create the route. A caller may add query parameters and a short path fragment (`_path`), never a different host; a parameter that collides with the injected credential is overwritten by it, and the caller's own headers are never forwarded.

The answer is the upstream's own status, content type and body, passed through unchanged.

Refusals say whose problem it is: `401` this install needs setting up again, `402` the developer's membership has lapsed (after a 30-day grace), `404` the developer turned the route off, `429` a rate ceiling, `502` the developer's key stopped working, `504` the upstream did not answer.

parameters.name: _path
parameters.description: Optional fragment appended to the developer's address. Letters, digits and / _ - . ~ only; `..` and a leading slash are refused.

schema.description: Passed through to the upstream unchanged, for routes the developer set to POST.

200.description: The upstream's answer, with its own status and content type.

post.description: Signs an unsigned `.shortcut` file via HubSign and streams back the signed file. Requires a HubSign API key (separate from the main key) and an active membership with HubSign access, unless called by an approved partner client.

The bundle must contain exactly one root SKILL.md with `name` + `description` YAML frontmatter. Limits: 25 files, 256 KB per file, 2 MB total; file types .md, .skill and .plugin only.

Send "0" to make it free (community). Omit to leave unchanged. Requires completed seller onboarding.

post.summary: MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0) — agents publish, fork and update registry items
post.description: A stateless Model Context Protocol endpoint over streamable HTTP. Point an MCP client (Claude Code, any agent framework) at this URL with your API key in the path. Supports initialize, tools/list and tools/call with 22 tools: search_registry, get_item, install_item, diff_versions, fork_item, publish_prompt, publish_cherri, publish_shortcut, publish_skill, publish_plugin, publish_version, set_price, set_license, list_my_items, propose_update, list_proposals, decide_proposal, provision_vm, get_vm, list_vms, destroy_vm, add_ssh_key. install_item returns the complete installable file set for anything you can access; publish_skill and publish_plugin upload whole bundles; publish_shortcut creates an Apple Shortcut listing from an iCloud share link you already have, and set_price also prices shortcuts (pass the numeric id as slug). Paid sources stay locked until purchased; forks carry permanent attribution; paid forks accrue a royalty to the original author. The five Boxes tools (members only) create, read, list and destroy your own Google Cloud VM and register SSH keys; they are hidden until the feature is switched on.

schema.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, ping).

post.summary: Set or clear an item's price
post.description: Change ONLY the price of a skill, prompt or plugin you own. Unlike the item's detail POST (which runs the full listing form, so any field you omit is blanked), this endpoint touches pricing and nothing else. Used by the `npx routinehub` CLI.

price_usd.description: Price as a plain 2-decimal string, e.g. "1.99" (minimum $0.99, maximum $100000). Amounts like "1.999" are rejected with 400. Send "0" to make the item free again.

payout.description: Required when price_usd > 0 and both payout rails are onboarded; otherwise the onboarded rail is used.

price_usd.description: null when the item is free.

post.description: Asks for a box and answers at once with the queued row; the machine comes up in about four minutes. Poll `GET /{api_key}/vm/{vm_id}` until `state` is `ready`, then use `ssh_command`. You need a registered SSH key first, one live box per member, and the site-wide and monthly-hours caps apply (429 when a cap is hit). JSON or form body.

shape.description: gpu-l4 only when GPU boxes are switched on.

ttl_hours.description: Clamped to 8; a longer request is never honoured.

post.description: One OpenSSH public key (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-sha2-*). It is placed on your next box under your username. Duplicates answer 409.

post.description: Called by the box itself, not by a member. The Bearer token is the box's own event token, minted with the box and useless anywhere else; a member API key is refused. A `vm.ready` event marks the box ready.

Returns an `rh_ik_` token the loader keeps in iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/RoutineHub/versions.json and sends as `Authorization: Bearer` to the app's front door. Rate-limited per IP and per app. Refusals answer in the loader contract: `{"verb": "done", "text": "..."}`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The shortcut version the loader reports (letters, digits, . _ -).

get.summary: Did this account buy this shortcut? (GET)
get.description: Public door for paid shortcuts (docs: https://routinehub.co/docs/proof-of-purchase/). Did the account behind this Proof of Purchase key buy this shortcut? The key goes in the `X-RH-Proof` header (or `Authorization: Bearer`), never in the URL. An Apple Shortcut cannot read the status code, so every answer carries `ok`, and every refusal carries an `error` sentence to show the buyer, plus `buy_url` where it helps. Counted: card purchases, crypto purchases, packs that hold the shortcut, the author, and a listing with no price. A refund or cancelled subscription flips the next answer to 402 by itself. The GET form takes the shortcut id as `?shortcut=`.

parameters.name: X-RH-Proof
parameters.description: The buyer's Proof of Purchase key, from routinehub.co/settings#api (the second key, under the developer key). Never a developer API key: that is refused with a 400 that says which key to paste.

200.description: The account bought it (or the listing is free, or the account is its author).

kind.description: What was found. `free`: the listing has no price, so everyone may run it. `author`: the account owns the listing.

expires_at.description: When a subscription or trial ends; null for a one-time purchase.

uses_left.description: Runs left on a pack of uses; null otherwise.

subject.description: A pseudonym for this buyer ON THIS SHORTCUT: stable for the pair, different on every other shortcut, never a username, unchanged when the key is regenerated.

400.description: Bad ask: no shortcut id, no such shortcut, a non-JSON body, or a developer API key pasted by mistake. `error` says which.

error.description: A sentence written to be shown to the buyer as-is.
error.example: No purchase of Battery Report found on this account.

401.description: The key is not valid, or its account is disabled. One message for both, on purpose.

error.description: A sentence written to be shown to the buyer as-is.

post.summary: Verify, and spend one run of a pack of uses
post.description: The same answer as `/proof-of-purchase/verify`, and when the purchase is a **pack of uses** it also spends one run: `uses_left` comes back one lower. Send your own `run_id` (any text up to 64 characters, unique per run); the same `run_id` twice spends nothing, so a retried run is never charged twice. An empty pack answers 402 with `buy_url`, and the buyer can buy another pack. For one-time and subscription purchases this behaves exactly like `/verify`.
